CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  January 17, 2025-2:20 P.M.
n  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING

  Pursuant to the Declaration of Local Emergency - Windstorms and Fires issued on January 8,
  2025 the meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.
  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 2:23 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Cole. (Absent:
  None)

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Councilmember Rick Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  Chief Assistant City Attorney Arnold Lee
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  Opening the meeting, Mayor Gordo reaffirmed the City's support for
  Altadena neighbors, and expressed his desire to uplift all impacted
  residents in Pasadena and Altadena as both communities navigate
  through this difficult time.

  ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO ALLOW THE CITY COUNCIL, ALL
  OF ITS OPERATING COMPANY BOARDS, AND THE PASADENA
  RENTAL HOUSING BOARD, TO MEET REMOTELY PURSUANT
  TO THE BROWN ACT (Office of the City Attorney)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is not a
  "project" subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and
  within the meaning ofCEQA Guidelines Section 15378(b); and
  (2) Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Pasadena
  authorizing Remote Teleconference Meetings of the City Council, all
  City operating company boards, and the Pasadena Rental Housing
  Board, for the period January 17, 2025 through February 12, 2025.
  (Resolution No. 10110)

  Chief Assistant City Attorney Lee introduced the item and reported
)
  that the proposed resolution would facilitate continuance of City
  business through remote meetings in a safe manner for all attendees
  of City Council, Operating Company boards, and the Pasadena

  Council Minutes  1  01/17/2025
   Rental Housing Board meetings, in compliance with Brown Act,
  under the local state of emergency.

  In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry regarding if City
  Committees and Commissions, and specifically City Council
  Committees, are included in the proposed resolution to meet
  remotely, City Manager Marquez reported that just the listed
  legislative bodies above are included in staff's recommendation due
  to the large number of advisory bodies that exist in the City, and the
  technological logistics of hosting and setting up virtual meetings.
  Philip Leclair, Chief Information Officer, reported that creating a
  virtual environment to host all committee and commission meetings
  could take a few weeks to set up.

  MOTION:  Following brief discussion, it was moved by Councilmember
  Hampton, seconded by Councilmember Jones, to approve the staff
  recommendation, amended to include City Council committees, and
  with direction to City staff to return with an analysis on including City
  Commissions at a later date.

  AYES: Councilmembers Cole, Hampton, Jones, Lyon,
  Madison, Masuda, Vice Mayor Rivas, Mayor Gordo
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION RATIFYING THE HEALTH
  OFFICER'S DECLARATION OF LOCAL HEALTH EMERGENCY
  DUE TO IMPACTS OF CRITICAL FIRE EVENTS AND
  WINDSTORM CONDITIONS IN THE CITY OF PASADENA
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is not a
  "project" subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and
  within the meaning of Section 15378(b); and
  (2) In accordance with Health and Safety Code section 101080,
  adopt a resolution ratifying the January 15, 2025, Health Officer
  Declaration of a Local hlealth Emergency due to impacts of critical
  fire events and windstorm conditions in the City of Pasadena.
  (Resolution No. 10111)

  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  RATIFYING THE CITY MANAGER'S POWER AIR BLOWER
  REGULATION (Office of the City Manager)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is not a
  "project" subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and
  within the meaning of Section 15378 (b); and

Council Minutes  2  01/17/2025
   (2) Adopt a Resolution ratifying the January 14, 2025 City Manager
  Power Air Blower Regulation. (Resolution No. 10112)

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, advocated for vulnerable community
  members working in post disaster recovery clean-up areas have
  access to personal protective equipment (PPE).

  APPROVE THE UPDATED WATER LEAK ASSISTANCE
  PROGRAM TO PROVIDE AID TO CUSTOMERS IMPACTED BY
  THE EATON FIRE AND AUTHORIZE THE GENERAL MANAGER
  OF THE WATER AND POWER DEPARTMENT TO MAKE
  ADJUSTMENTS TO WATER UTILITY BILLS FOR HIGH USAGE
  (Water & Power Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that this action proposed in the agenda report is not a
  "project" subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and
  within the meaning of Section 15378(b);
  (2) Approve the updated Water Leak Assistance Program to provide
  aid to customers impacted by the Eaton Fire; and
  (3) Authorize the General Manager (or designee) of the Water and
  Power Department to adjust water utility bills for high usage due to
  the impacts of the Eaton Fire.

  AUTHORIZE THE GENERAL MANAGER OF THE WATER AND
  POWER DEPARTMENT TO PAUSE OR SUSPEND THE UTILITY
  BILLING PROCESS AS A RESPONSE TO THE 2025 EATON
  WILDFIRE DISASTER
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is not a
  "project" subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and
  within the meaning of Section 15378(b); and
  (2) Authorize the General Manager (or designee) of the Water and
  Power Department to temporarily:
  a. Pause the billing process for water and electric sen/ices for
  customers whose account was closed due to the loss of their
  home or business in the 2025 Eaton Wildfire Disaster;
  b. Suspend collection of late fees for up to 60 days for customers
  who were displaced during a mandatory evacuation caused
  by the 2025 Eaton Wildfire Disaster; and
  c. Suspend service interruptions due to non-payment for up to
  60 days for customers who were displaced during a
  mandatory evacuation caused by the 2025 Eaton Wildfire
  Disaster.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that two letters related to Item 4,
  expressing concerns related to local air quality during the disaster
  recovery and advocating for the implementation of safety measures,
  was received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City

Council Minutes  3  01/17/2025
   Council, posted online, and made part of the public record for the
  item.

  MOTION:  It was moved by Councilmember Cole, seconded by Councilmember
  Hampton, to approve the staff recommendations for Items 4-7.

  AYES: Councilmembers Cole, Hampton, Jones, Lyon,
  Madison, Masuda, Vice Mayor Rivas, Mayor Gordo
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  UPDATE - CITY RESPONSE TO WINDSTORMS AND FIRES -
  CITY MANAGER AND EMERGENCY OPERATIONS STAFF
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Consider updates from City staff and provide direction if desired
  by the City Council; and
  (2) Find that, if direction is given to staff, it would not be a "project"
  subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and within the
  meaning of CEQA Guidelines Section 15378(b).

  Chad Augustin, Fire Chief, provided a status update on the Eaton
  Fire. He stated that over 8,500 structures have been searched, all
  Pasadena residents have been accounted for, and no Pasadena
  residents have suffered a fatality as a result of the wildfire. He also
  noted that the City is working with Cal Fire to prepare for future mud
  and debris flow should a rainstorm occur.

  Mayor Gordo reported that he met with mayors of various cities in
  the San Gabriel Valley and noted their offers of assistance to the
  City, and that some have already provided resources and other
  assistance.

  In response to Mayor Gordo's inquiry regarding the two major power
  transmission lines serving the City, David Reyes, Acting General
  Manager of Water and Power, reported that the Gould Line was
  affected by the Eaton Fire (temporarily non-operational), while the
  Mesa Line is still operating, and also noted that the Glenarm power
  plant is operating as a back-up energy source to the Mesa Line.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry regarding the
  longest power outage, Acting General Manager Reyes noted that the
  longest outage was approximately 5 days and was located in a
  mandatory evacuation zone. Councilmember Hampton thanked City
  crews for restoring service in a quick and safe manner, despite not
  being able to perform work in mandatory evacuation zones.

Council Minutes  4  01/17/2025
   Councilmember Jones suggested the City staff assess damaged
  water infrastructure in Altadena and have the City partner with public
  utilities in the fire zone to help the neighboring area restore water
  service in the near future, repair and preserve important
  infrastructure and resources, and protect fire victims from having to
  sell their properties to large developers due to a lack of water
  resources/infrastructure.

  Councilmember Cole advocated for the City Council to consider
  ways to assist Altadena businesses, including helping those that
  may want to temporarily relocate to Pasadena in vacant spaces.

  Mayor Gordo suggested moving up the date for the joint meeting with
  LA County Supervisor Kathryn Barger and extending invitations to
Councilmember Masuda  the Altadena Town Council to discuss recovery efforts.
left the meeting at 3:50
p.m. due to technological  Manuel Carmona, Acting Director of Pasadena Public Health
difficulties.  Department, provided a status update on the norovirus outbreak at
  the evacuation shelter at Pasadena Convention Center. He further
  reported that the City's Health Department is working with the
  American Red Cross, Kaiser Permanente, and AltaMed to deploy
  prevention and control measures at the shelter including the
  development of isolation halls and increased sanitation efforts for
  shelter residents.

  In response to Councilmember Cole's inquiry regarding the status of
  air quality, Dr. Parveen Kaur, Acting Health Officer, stated that air
  quality testing and status may take time to accurately measure, and
  advised the public to wear personal protective equipment such as
  N95 masks to guard against pollutants. Acting Director of Public
  Health Carmona also clarified that the City has not issued a mask
  mandate, but is only suggesting that the public wear masks due to
  air quality affected by fire and smoke.

  Discussion ensued regarding recommendations for masking, safe
  air quality, and potential risks for youth to be outside.

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for the City to conduct air
  quality testing, and Councilmember Cole requested that staff
  agendize air quality testing for further discussion to provide the
  public with an opportunity to comment on the matter.

  In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry regarding green waste
  pickup and the impacts on street parking, Public Works Director
  Greg de Vinck reported that City crews have been consistently
Councilmember Masuda
  working on clearing tree and brush debris, and that contracts were
returned to the meeting at  recently issued to bring in additional trucks and larger equipment to
4:11 p.m.
  collect larger pieces of debris. He added that the City will be
  contracting with local labor for debris cleanup work.

Council Minutes  5  01/17/2025
   Acting Public Health Director Carmona reported that the Public
  Health building at 1845 N Fair Oaks Ave will reopen for individuals
  impacted by the Eaton Fire to assist them obtaining vital records.

  Joaquin Siques, Director of Transportation, briefly reported on
  upcoming resumption of parking enforcement for street parking and
  City-owned lots to promote turnover for businesses. He also noted
  that City staff will be returning to the City Council with a report
  regarding overnight parking and fees for those impacted by the
  Eaton Fire.

  Discussion ensued regarding pre-approved building plans for ADUs
  and single-family residences, maximizing opportunities for impacted
  residents to rebuild, and the need to expedite the plan check and
  permit approval process for homes with customizations as well.

  Councilmember Masuda requested City staff to release an updated
  map regarding the water quality in Upper Hastings Ranch.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that the one letter advocating for a rent
  freeze and/or eviction moratorium as a result of the impacts of the
  Eaton Fire, and two letters requesting the City waive Measure H City
  Charter provisions and other related comments, were received by
  the City Clerk's office, distributed to the City Council, posted online,
  and made part of the public record for this item.

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, advocated for the Legislative Policy
  Committee to review and discuss State disaster relief bills
  related to the LA fires and implementing an ad hoc task force as
  partofAB239.

  Brook Perez, residence not stated, commended the City for the
  handling of the Eaton fire and the quick actions to establish of
  the evacuation center at the Pasadena Convention Center.

  Ash Riveire, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns regarding
  the displacement of tenants and advocated for an eviction
  moratorium and rent freezes to prevent price gouging.

  Following discussion, the City Council provided the following
  direction to City staff: 1) explore the possibility of moving up the joint
  meeting with LA County Supervisor Kathryn Barger and invite the
  Altadena Town Council, 2) have Pasadena Water and Power check
  on water infrastructure in Altadena, 3) explore air testing around
  burn sites and check in with AQMD, 4) continue emphasis on debris
  removal efforts and explore local support from non-profits and other
  local entities, 5) start work on expedited home and ADD
  construction, including streamlined permitting and plan check
  processes to help facilitate rebuilding, and 6) provided an updated
  map depicting water quality in Upper Hastings Ranch.

Council Minutes  6  01/17/2025
   ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the special meeting of the City Council
